_comment: Where to look for jobs. Edit feeds/searches freely. Remote-only: every search below carries the source's own remote filter; antiKeywords in skills.json push down on-site/hybrid postings that slip through.
_minScoreComment: Cold applications must clear a HIGH bar (much stricter than inbound replies) so you only apply to strong frontend matches, not spray-and-pray. Raise to be pickier, lower for more results.
_candidateCountryComment: Where the candidate lives and works remotely from — every spelling the boards use (English + local). Drives two things: the LLM gate scores a vacancy open only to residents of OTHER countries (or requiring relocation / an office abroad) at most 10, and Djinni's countries segment ('Тільки віддалено · Канада, Польща, Сербія') must name one of these or the whole world. The first entry is used in the English LLM prompt.
_alsoCountriesComment: Countries besides candidateCountry that suit the candidate just as well (a vacancy open to residents of any of them is as good as one open to the home country). Key = English name (the LLM prompt names it), value = the boards' other spellings (Djinni writes 'Румунія'). They join candidateCountry for Djinni's countries segment, Himalayas / Telegram eligibility and the dashboard's 'listed' mark, and they are told to the LLM gate. Himalayas still asks its API only for the home country (the first candidateCountry entry). Leave out of excludeLocation too.
_excludeTitleComment: Job titles containing any of these whole words are skipped before scoring (no application package), across all sources. Used to drop entry-level roles and manual-only QA. Matched in the title only (Latin words, whole-word), so senior roles that merely mention these words in the description are kept.
_excludeFullstackStackComment: Dealbreaker languages for FULLSTACK vacancies. A vacancy whose title says full stack / fullstack / фулстек is dropped before scoring when its title or description names any of these as a whole word — a Node/TypeScript fullstack role is the target, a Java/PHP/Python/Go one is not. Pure frontend and Node.js-only roles are never touched by this. Matching is case-insensitive, except a term written WITH a capital letter, which is matched exactly: 'Go' must not hit the verb ('Go beyond…' at the start of a sentence is skipped too), while 'golang' is unambiguous and matches any case. 'java' does not match JavaScript. The whole text counts, not only a 'Requirements' section: a language named as a nice-to-have drops the vacancy too. A card whose description failed to load has only its title to match, so it falls through to the normal gate. Set to [] to switch the rule off.
_excludeLocationComment: Boards also list vacancies physically located abroad (DOU marks them 'за кордоном', Djinni 'Тільки офіс · Польща' etc). Jobs whose location contains any of these substrings (case-insensitive) are dropped across ALL sources before scoring.
_llmComment: LLM re-scoring + tailored cover letters via the local Claude CLI (claude -p). Keyword minScore/requireRole decide what reaches the LLM; when the LLM answers with a fit score below llm.minScore (0–100) the job is dropped as low instead of getting a package. A verdict below minScore but at or above borderlineMin (default 50; 0 turns the band off) is written as a `tier: borderline` package — a muted Borderline tab on the dashboard, no Telegram message — because the cutoff is noisy by about ±12 points. A failed or timed-out verdict defers the job to the next run; a second failure writes a keyword-only package into the same Borderline tab (never lose a match to an outage). Set minScore to 0 to make the LLM advisory-only. maxPerRun caps CLI calls per run. `model` is the claude CLI alias (sonnet by default: stricter on weak fits and ~2x faster than haiku); `concurrency` = parallel CLI calls per run (default 3); `timeoutSec` (default 60, min 30) kills a call that runs longer; good calls take ~8 s (p50) and the log line `llm: verdict in N s` shows yours, so a hung call is given up after one minute instead of three.

dou._comment: Official DOU RSS feeds. ?remote keeps only remote-friendly postings; category/search mirror the site's filters.

djinni._comment: Public Djinni jobs board, read with a plain fetch (no login, no browser). Each search is a full jobs-search URL — copy them from your browser's filters (set 'Remote' there and copy the URL if the employment param ever changes). primary_keyword=JavaScript is Djinni's front-end category; Fullstack and Node.js widen the net. fullDescription (default true) follows each job link for the complete text so scoring is accurate; set false to score on the listing snippet only. pages (default 3): Djinni does not list newest-first, so each search reads this many pages of 15. concurrency (default 5): parallel detail-page fetches.

himalayas._comment: Himalayas remote-jobs board (https://himalayas.app) via its free public JSON API — no key, no login, no browser. Foreign employers hiring remotely. Each search is a free-text query; the API itself keeps only jobs open to the FIRST candidateCountry entry (use its English name) or to the whole world, newest first. pages (default 2): pages of up to 20 read per search. worldwide (default true): false keeps only jobs that name the candidate's country itself and drops the ones open to the whole world, which draw applicants from everywhere.

tgchannels._comment: Public Telegram job channels, read through their web preview (https://t.me/s/<channel>) — no login, no bot, no browser. Only channels have a preview: a group (members, not subscribers) is reported and skipped. Posts must use the 'Field: value' template @remote_qa_jobs uses (Title, Company name, Location, Anywhere, …); a post without a Title is skipped. Location / Anywhere decide eligibility like Djinni's countries: the candidate's country or the whole world; worldwide (default true): false keeps only posts whose Location names the candidate's country itself. fullDescription (default true) fetches each new job's apply link for the full JSON-LD description — the post's own summary is too short for the LLM gate. pages (default 1): pages of ~20 posts read per channel. Unrelated to telegram.json, which sends your own alerts to your phone. Disabled: the only channel known to use that template is @remote_qa_jobs (QA roles); add a front-end/fullstack channel here, then set enabled to true.

linkedin._comment: Scraping LinkedIn job search violates ToS and is more detectable. Kept modest: few results, polite delays. remote:true adds the f_WT=2 filter. Locations cover the target markets: Greece (home), EU, US — all remote. Set enabled=false to turn off.
